assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
attention is approximated by obtainable public signals (search interest, follower counts, news/Wikipedia volume), not by the unobservable latent construct
the region hierarchy is a finite closed tree with single-parent containment so the node universe is enumerable
salience is perishable: the map is valid only over a stated short validity window derived from estimated half-life
exclusions: private platform analytics and non-public attention signals
individual-level surveillance or person-tracking (only aggregate place/entity salience)
causal claims that attention salience equals economic or political importance
real-time streaming inference (the method snapshots and re-pulls, it does not stream)
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for geographic and demographic attention-topology work units, informed by Zipf rank-size law, Christaller central place theory, Rogers diffusion of innovations, Barabasi-Albert scale-free networks, the Simon/Davenport-Beck attention economy, and Anderson long-tail economics; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Zipf 1949 Human Behavior and the Principle of Least Effort (rank-size law); Christaller 1933 Central Places in Southern Germany (central place theory); Rogers 2003 Diffusion of Innovations (5th ed.); Barabasi & Albert 1999 'Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks' (Science); Simon 1971 'Designing Organizations for an Information-Rich World' and Davenport & Beck 2001 The Attention Economy; Anderson 2006 The Long Tail; Clauset, Shalizi & Newman 2009 'Power-law distributions in empirical data'

competency_questions.question: How is the finite region hierarchy defined and kept enumerable with single-parent containment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGION_TAXONOMY defines the closed country>state>city hierarchy with market tiers

competency_questions.question: What public signals feed the salience metric and how are they acquired with provenance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALIENCE_METRIC defines the weighted signal aggregate; SIGNAL_SOURCING acquires and stamps each datum

competency_questions.question: How is salience quantified and normalized so unequal-size regions are comparable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALIENCE_METRIC scores attention; SALIENCE_NORMALIZATION makes scores comparable across levels

competency_questions.question: How is platform-skewed visibility distinguished from true regional salience?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAMPLING_BIAS profiles per-platform skew and re-weights signals

competency_questions.question: What is the expected attention structure across the hierarchy and its theoretical grounding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RANK_SIZE_DISTRIBUTION fits Zipf concentration; CENTRAL_PLACE_STRUCTURE supplies the Christaller prior

competency_questions.question: How concentrated is attention and what link topology and tail cutoff describe it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RANK_SIZE_DISTRIBUTION and SCALE_FREE_LINKAGE characterize concentration; LONG_TAIL_CUTOFF sets the head/tail boundary

competency_questions.question: How does salience decay over time and how is the map's validity window derived?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ATTENTION_HALF_LIFE estimates decay; DIFFUSION_DYNAMICS models spread

competency_questions.question: How is the seed region chosen and the traversal anchored to it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEED_SELECTION justifies the start region; EXPANSION_FRONTIER anchors the traversal

competency_questions.question: How does the traversal expand regions in decreasing salience order and stay bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPANSION_FRONTIER expands in decreasing-salience order; DEPTH_BREADTH_BOUNDS bounds it

competency_questions.question: How are frontier size and per-node fan-out capped so the web is finite and terminates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEPTH_BREADTH_BOUNDS caps frontier/budget; TOPK_FANOUT and LONG_TAIL_CUTOFF bound fan-out and tail

competency_questions.question: How are cross-border diaspora communities modeled as bridges and how does attention diffuse across them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIASPORA_BRIDGES adds cross-subtree bridge edges; DIFFUSION_DYNAMICS models spread along them

competency_questions.question: How is the map kept fresh against decay through scheduled re-pulls?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STALENESS_REVISIT schedules half-life-driven re-pulls feeding REPRODUCIBILITY snapshots

competency_questions.question: How is reproducibility and overall web completeness/finiteness validated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPRODUCIBILITY pins inputs for deterministic rebuilds; COVERAGE_VALIDATION certifies finiteness and order

glossary.definition: a scalar attention score for a place/entity aggregated from weighted public signals
the finite closed tree of country>state>city units with single-parent containment
Zipf's regularity that the rank-r place's salience is about s(1)/r^a
the time over which a place's salience decays to half its value
the salience-keyed priority queue of unvisited nodes awaiting expansion
the cap on how many highest-salience neighbors a node enqueues
a cross-border edge linking region subtrees via a salient migrant community
the many low-salience places below the head/tail cutoff whose aggregate weight can rival the head
the short time span over which the attention map is declared current

nodes.definition: Define the finite, closed hierarchy of geographic and demographic units the attention web is built over: country -> state/province -> city/metro, with market tiers (tier-1/2/3) attached, so every place has exactly one parent and the universe of nodes is enumerable and bounded.

base.update_signal: administrative boundaries redrawn or a new market-tier scheme adopted

pros.claim: A closed single-parent hierarchy guarantees the node universe is finite and traversal terminates
pros.example: India>Punjab>Ludhiana is one path; no place has two parents

cons.claim: Rigid administrative nesting hides cross-cutting demographic communities that ignore borders
cons.example: a metro area that spans two states is forced into one parent

failure_modes: overlapping or multi-parent regions break containment
unbounded 'neighborhood' granularity explodes the node set
acceptance_tests: every region resolves to exactly one parent and the full set is enumerable and finite
revisit_triggers: administrative boundaries change
a needed granularity level is missing from the hierarchy

nodes.definition: Specify the scalar salience score s(place) = weighted aggregate of obtainable public attention signals (Google Trends search interest, follower/subscriber counts, news article volume, Wikipedia pageviews), with explicit signal weights and units, so attention is a measurable quantity rather than a hunch.

base.update_signal: a signal source's API or methodology changes, or signal weights are revised

pros.claim: A defined, weighted metric makes salience reproducible and comparable across places
pros.example: s = 0.4*trends + 0.3*log(followers) + 0.2*news_volume + 0.1*pageviews

cons.claim: Public signals proxy attention imperfectly; the metric measures visibility, not the latent construct
cons.example: a place with no search-trends coverage scores low despite real local attention

failure_modes: a single dominant signal swamps the aggregate
signals with incomparable units summed without normalization
acceptance_tests: s(place) is computable from named public sources and reproduces to within tolerance on re-pull
weights are documented and sum to a fixed total
revisit_triggers: a signal source is deprecated
the weighting scheme is challenged by observed bias

nodes.definition: Normalize raw salience so unequal-size regions are comparable: divide by or regress out population/baseline-volume, convert to per-capita or z-scored attention, so a small high-intensity place is not always dominated by a large low-intensity one.

base.update_signal: the population/baseline denominator or normalization scheme changes

pros.claim: Normalization lets a small region with intense per-capita attention compete with a populous one
pros.example: a small diaspora hub outranks a large city on per-capita salience

cons.claim: Over-normalizing can erase the genuine mass-attention advantage of large hubs
cons.example: per-capita scoring makes a megacity look unremarkable

failure_modes: normalizing by a stale population figure distorts ranks
mixing normalized and raw scores in one ranking
acceptance_tests: scores are comparable across levels: two regions with equal per-capita attention receive equal normalized scores
revisit_triggers: population baselines are updated
a normalization artifact inverts an expected rank

nodes.definition: Acquire the raw public attention signals that feed the salience metric from obtainable sources (Google Trends, platform follower counts, GDELT/news volume, Wikipedia pageview API), recording source, timestamp, and access method for each datum.

base.update_signal: a source's terms of service, rate limit, or schema changes

pros.claim: Stamping each datum with source and timestamp makes the whole web auditable and re-pullable
pros.example: every follower count carries the platform and the UTC pull time

cons.claim: Public APIs rate-limit and change schemas, so sourcing is the most fragile layer
cons.example: Google Trends caps query volume and rescales to 0-100 per query window

failure_modes: a source rate-limit silently truncates coverage
un-timestamped data cannot be reproduced or revisited
acceptance_tests: each signal datum carries source id, timestamp, and access method and can be re-pulled
sourcing covers all regions at the seed level
revisit_triggers: a source API changes
coverage gaps appear for a region level

nodes.definition: Resolve which place/entity each public signal actually refers to before it is scored: disambiguate homonymous place names, language variants, and entity-vs-place collisions (e.g. search interest for 'Punjab' spanning India, Pakistan, and namesake places abroad) so a signal is attributed to the correct hierarchy node.

base.update_signal: a naming/geocoding scheme changes or a new homonym collision is found

pros.claim: Correct attribution stops one node's salience from being inflated by a homonym's signal
pros.example: 'Punjab' search interest is split between the Indian and Pakistani regions, not summed onto one

cons.claim: Disambiguation needs a gazetteer/geocoder whose coverage and recency are themselves uncertain
cons.example: a small place absent from the gazetteer is mis-attributed to its larger homonym

failure_modes: homonymous signals merged onto one node
language variants of a place name counted as separate places
acceptance_tests: every scored signal is attributed to exactly one hierarchy node via a documented disambiguation rule
revisit_triggers: the gazetteer/geocoding scheme changes
a homonym mis-attribution is detected in residuals

nodes.definition: Characterize and correct platform-skewed visibility: the signals measure what a platform surfaces, not true salience. Identify per-platform demographic and geographic skews (age, language, urban tilt) and down-weight or re-balance signals accordingly.

base.update_signal: platform demographics shift or a new dominant platform emerges in a region

pros.claim: Modeling platform skew separates 'platform visibility' from 'true regional attention'
pros.example: a youth-skewed platform is down-weighted when scoring an older-demographic region

cons.claim: Bias correction needs a ground-truth demographic baseline that is itself uncertain
cons.example: census language data lags actual diaspora language use

failure_modes: uncorrected urban/English-language tilt inflates already-visible places
over-correction invents attention where a platform simply is absent
acceptance_tests: each platform signal carries a documented skew profile and a correction factor before aggregation
known coverage gaps are flagged not silently zero-filled
revisit_triggers: a platform's user base shifts demographically
a systematic geographic bias is detected in residuals

nodes.definition: Fit the rank-size (Zipf / power-law) distribution of salience across places and entities within a level: rank r places have salience approximately s(1)/r^a. Estimate the exponent a, validate the heavy tail, and use it to predict how concentrated attention is.

base.update_signal: the fitted Zipf exponent drifts or the distribution stops being heavy-tailed

pros.claim: A Zipfian fit quantifies attention concentration and predicts the few hubs that dominate
pros.example: top-3 cities hold most national attention, matching exponent a~1, per Zipf 1949

cons.claim: Naive power-law fitting overstates tails; many distributions are lognormal, not strictly Zipfian
cons.example: a maximum-likelihood fit per Clauset et al. rejects power-law for some levels

failure_modes: fitting a power law where the data is lognormal misstates concentration
ignoring finite-size cutoff at the tail
acceptance_tests: the rank-size fit reproduces on re-pull and passes a tail goodness-of-fit threshold
the exponent is reported with a confidence interval
revisit_triggers: the exponent drifts beyond its interval
goodness-of-fit rejects the heavy-tail assumption

nodes.definition: Model the attention web's link topology as scale-free: salient hubs attract disproportionately many links (preferential attachment, Barabasi-Albert 1999), producing a few high-degree attention hubs and many low-degree places. Use degree distribution to identify structural hubs distinct from raw-salience leaders.

base.update_signal: the link-formation model or degree-distribution assumption changes

pros.claim: Scale-free structure explains why a handful of hubs mediate most cross-region attention flow
pros.example: a single diaspora-hub city links dozens of smaller regions, per Barabasi-Albert 1999

cons.claim: Real attention networks deviate from pure preferential attachment; degree alone misranks bridges
cons.example: a low-degree but high-betweenness place is a critical bridge the model under-weights

failure_modes: treating degree as the only hub signal hides high-betweenness bridges
assuming pure BA growth ignores aging/fitness of attention
acceptance_tests: the degree distribution is heavy-tailed and identified hubs overlap with high-salience leaders on a sanity check
revisit_triggers: the topology stops being scale-free
a critical bridge is mis-ranked by degree alone

nodes.definition: Model the temporal decay of salience: attention is perishable and follows an exponential-like decay with a place/topic-specific half-life (Simon 1971 scarce attention; Davenport-Beck 2001). Estimate the half-life so the map is declared valid only over a short, stated time window.

base.update_signal: observed decay rate changes or a viral spike resets the half-life

pros.claim: A measured half-life turns 'the map is stale' into a quantitative validity window
pros.example: a news-driven spike decays with a 9-day half-life, so the map is valid ~2 weeks

cons.claim: A single half-life hides bimodal decay: a fast news component plus a slow baseline
cons.example: a celebrity's baseline followers persist while their news spike vanishes

failure_modes: assuming a single decay rate misstates validity for mixed signals
ignoring decay yields a confidently wrong stale map
acceptance_tests: each place/topic carries an estimated half-life and a derived validity window
decayed signals below threshold are flagged, not used as current
revisit_triggers: a viral event resets decay dynamics
measured decay diverges from the fitted model

nodes.definition: Choose the seed region the traversal starts from (e.g. Punjab, the USA, or a specific major city), justified by salience, coverage, and the analysis goal, since the seed anchors the whole expansion and biases what the web emphasizes.

base.update_signal: the analysis goal or the seed's own salience materially changes

pros.claim: A justified, salience-anchored seed makes the web's emphasis explicit and reproducible
pros.example: seeding at Punjab makes diaspora bridges to Canada/UK first-class, not incidental

cons.claim: Seed choice biases the entire map; a different seed yields a different attention web
cons.example: seeding at the USA buries a regionally salient but globally minor place

failure_modes: an arbitrary seed produces a web that does not reflect the stated goal
seed lacks signal coverage, starving the traversal
acceptance_tests: the seed is justified against salience and goal, and has full signal coverage at its level
revisit_triggers: the analysis goal changes
the seed's salience rank shifts materially

nodes.definition: Traverse the region/entity space in strictly DECREASING salience (size/hype) order: maintain a priority frontier keyed by salience, always expand the most salient unvisited node next, so the most important attention is mapped first and the order is deterministic.

base.update_signal: the traversal order key or priority semantics change

pros.claim: Decreasing-order traversal maps the highest-attention regions first and is deterministic given the salience scores
pros.example: the frontier pops the top city before any tier-3 town, like a best-first search

cons.claim: Pure greedy salience order can starve structurally important but low-salience bridge nodes
cons.example: a low-salience but high-betweenness bridge is visited late or never under the bound

failure_modes: non-deterministic tie-breaking makes the traversal irreproducible
greedy order strands critical bridges below the frontier cutoff
acceptance_tests: the traversal expands nodes in strictly non-increasing salience order with deterministic tie-breaking
re-running the traversal on the same scores yields the same order
revisit_triggers: the priority key definition changes
a critical bridge is consistently stranded by greedy order

nodes.definition: Cap the frontier size and the per-node top_k fan-out (and total node budget / max depth) so the traversal provably terminates and the web stays finite, converting potential unbounded expansion into an explicit, handleable stop condition.

base.update_signal: the node budget, top_k, max-depth, or frontier cap policy changes

pros.claim: Explicit caps guarantee finite, terminating traversal and bound compute cost
pros.example: top_k=5 per node and a 500-node budget cap the entire web's size

cons.claim: Caps set too tight truncate salient regions; too loose let the web explode toward the long tail
cons.example: a top_k=2 cap drops the 3rd-ranked but still-salient neighbor, per Anderson 2006 long tail

failure_modes: a cap set below true required breadth drops salient nodes
an unbounded fan-out lets the long tail explode the node set
acceptance_tests: every traversal terminates within the node budget and max depth with explicit caps
exceeding a cap raises a documented stop/defeater, not a crash
revisit_triggers: the bound policy changes
truncation of a salient region is observed at the cap boundary

nodes.definition: At each expanded node, select the top_k highest-salience neighbors/children to enqueue, so fan-out is bounded and only the most salient links propagate, implementing the long-tail cutoff (Anderson 2006) at the local level.

base.update_signal: the top_k value or neighbor-ranking rule changes

pros.claim: Local top_k selection bounds branching and keeps only the most salient neighbors
pros.example: a city enqueues its 5 most-salient linked places and drops the long tail

cons.claim: A fixed top_k ignores that some hubs legitimately have more salient neighbors than others
cons.example: a top global hub with 20 salient links is cut to k=5, losing real structure

failure_modes: a uniform top_k under-serves true hubs and over-serves leaves
ties at the kth position broken non-deterministically
acceptance_tests: each expanded node enqueues exactly its top_k normalized-salience neighbors with deterministic tie-breaks
revisit_triggers: the top_k policy changes
a true hub is observed to be over-truncated by a uniform k

nodes.definition: Model diaspora and cross-border salient communities as bridge nodes/edges that link otherwise-separate region subtrees (e.g. Punjabi communities linking India, Canada, the UK), since attention diffuses across borders through these communities (Rogers 2003 diffusion of innovations).

base.update_signal: a diaspora community's size or cross-border activity changes materially

excluded: single-parent containment (bridges are extra edges, not re-parenting)

pros.claim: Bridge edges capture real cross-border attention diffusion the strict hierarchy cannot
pros.example: a Punjabi diaspora bridge carries attention from Ludhiana to Brampton and back

cons.claim: Bridges can re-introduce cycles and weaken the finite-hierarchy guarantee if added carelessly
cons.example: a bridge that re-parents a region breaks single-parent containment

failure_modes: a bridge that creates a containment cycle
over-broad bridges that merge unrelated regions
acceptance_tests: bridges are added as non-containment edges only and never re-parent a region
each bridge cites an identifiable cross-border community
revisit_triggers: a diaspora community's cross-border salience shifts
a bridge is found to merge unrelated regions

nodes.definition: Ground the region hierarchy's expected attention structure in central place theory (Christaller): higher-order central places serve and out-attract their lower-order hinterlands, giving a prior on parent-vs-child salience that the empirical web can be checked against.

base.update_signal: the central-place prior conflicts repeatedly with observed salience

excluded: empirical scoring (this is a prior to check against)

pros.claim: Christaller's hierarchy gives a theory-based prior on which places should dominate their hinterland
pros.example: a regional capital is expected to out-attract its surrounding towns

cons.claim: Central place theory assumes economic-service gravity that attention can violate in the social-media era
cons.example: a small town goes viral and out-attracts its regional capital

failure_modes: forcing the Christaller prior over contradicting data hides genuine viral inversions
treating the prior as ground truth instead of a checkable expectation
acceptance_tests: the central-place prior is recorded as an expectation and deviations from observed salience are flagged, not overwritten
revisit_triggers: observed salience repeatedly inverts the central-place prior
the hinterland grouping no longer matches administrative reality

nodes.definition: Model how attention spreads through the web over time using diffusion-of-innovations dynamics (Rogers 2003): innovators/early-adopter hubs ignite, attention propagates along bridges and high-degree links following an S-curve, informing which neighbors will become salient next.

base.update_signal: the diffusion model parameters or adopter-category mapping change

pros.claim: Diffusion dynamics predict which low-salience neighbor is about to rise, guiding pre-emptive re-pull
pros.example: a hub's spike forecasts its bridged diaspora region rising next, per Rogers 2003

cons.claim: Diffusion forecasts are noisy and often wrong at the individual-place level
cons.example: an expected cascade fizzles because the bridge community is dormant

failure_modes: overfitting an S-curve to a short window mis-forecasts the cascade
ignoring the late-majority plateau misreads saturation as decline
acceptance_tests: diffusion forecasts are scored against subsequent observed salience and recalibrated when they miss
revisit_triggers: forecast accuracy degrades
the adopter-category mapping no longer fits observed propagation

nodes.definition: Schedule re-pulls of salience signals driven by the estimated half-life: when a place's signal age exceeds a decay threshold, re-acquire and re-score it, so the map tracks attention as it moves rather than freezing at first capture.

base.update_signal: the decay threshold or re-pull scheduling policy changes

pros.claim: Half-life-driven re-pulls keep the map current without re-pulling everything every run
pros.example: a 9-day half-life place is re-pulled biweekly; a stable place yearly

cons.claim: Aggressive re-pulling burns API budget; lazy re-pulling lets the map drift stale
cons.example: re-pulling every place daily exhausts rate limits

failure_modes: a fixed re-pull interval ignores per-place half-life
re-pull thrashing on a noisy signal
acceptance_tests: any place whose signal age exceeds its decay threshold is queued for re-pull before the map is served as current
revisit_triggers: the decay threshold policy changes
stale places are observed being served as current

nodes.definition: Define the cutoff that separates the salient head from the long tail (Anderson 2006): a salience or rank threshold below which places are excluded from the web, keeping the map finite while documenting what the tail omits.

base.update_signal: the head/tail cutoff threshold or its rationale changes

pros.claim: An explicit head/tail cutoff bounds the map and makes omissions transparent
pros.example: include places above the 95th salience percentile; document the omitted tail count

cons.claim: A cutoff hides the aggregate weight of the long tail, which can rival the head (Anderson 2006)
cons.example: thousands of tiny places together hold attention the head-only map ignores

failure_modes: a cutoff that drops a place which later goes viral
an undocumented cutoff makes omissions invisible
acceptance_tests: the cutoff threshold and the count/weight of omitted tail places are documented and reproducible
revisit_triggers: the cutoff threshold changes
aggregate tail weight is found to rival the head

nodes.definition: Guarantee that the same inputs (signal snapshot, weights, bounds, seed) deterministically produce the same attention web: pin signal snapshots, fix random tie-breaks, version all parameters, so any run is byte-reproducible from its manifest.

base.update_signal: the manifest schema or the set of pinned inputs changes

pros.claim: A pinned manifest makes the whole web byte-reproducible and auditable
pros.example: re-running from manifest v3 yields an identical web months later

cons.claim: Strict pinning fights freshness: a reproducible snapshot is by definition not live
cons.example: the reproducible map is a frozen past, not today's attention

failure_modes: unpinned signals make the web irreproducible
a hidden time/random dependency breaks determinism
acceptance_tests: the same manifest produces a byte-identical web on re-run
every parameter and signal snapshot is versioned in the manifest
revisit_triggers: the manifest schema changes
a non-deterministic dependency is discovered in a run

nodes.definition: Validate the finished attention web: it is finite, every node is reachable from the seed under the bounds, salience order is respected, the head/tail cutoff and omissions are documented, and the map carries its validity window. This closes the method against the stated purpose.

base.update_signal: the completeness/validity acceptance definition changes

pros.claim: A single completeness gate certifies the web is finite, ordered, reproducible, and time-bounded
pros.example: the gate confirms 482 nodes, all seed-reachable, salience-ordered, valid 14 days

cons.claim: Completeness over the modeled universe can still miss attention the signals never captured
cons.example: a region salient only on an unmonitored platform is absent yet the web passes

failure_modes: passing completeness on a biased signal set certifies a biased map
skipping the validity-window check serves a stale web as current
acceptance_tests: the web passes finiteness, seed-reachability, salience-order, cutoff-documentation, and validity-window checks before it is served
revisit_triggers: the acceptance definition changes
a passing web is later found to omit a known-salient region

edges.why_related: re-pulled signals feed back to recompute the salience metric for aged places
a forecast cascade triggers a pre-emptive re-pull of the predicted-rising neighbor
the central-place prior constrains expected expansion order and flags inversions
platform skew corrections enter as adjustments before normalization compares regions
bridge edges add cross-subtree neighbors the frontier may expand out of strict containment order

edges.resolution_rule: treat bias correction as a documented adjustment layer applied before aggregation: the raw metric stays auditable while the corrected score drives ranking, so neither raw visibility nor an unverifiable correction silently wins
edges.why_related: raw public signals measure platform visibility while bias correction claims true salience; the two pull the score in opposite directions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the attention web

edges.resolution_rule: expand in strict decreasing-salience order but stop at the bound; when the bound would strand a high-betweenness bridge, raise a documented defeater rather than silently dropping it or removing the bound
edges.why_related: greedy decreasing-salience traversal wants to keep expanding while the finite-frontier bound forces termination, risking stranded structurally-important nodes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the attention web

edges.resolution_rule: serve from a pinned snapshot for reproducibility and attach its validity window; trigger a re-pull and a new versioned snapshot when age exceeds the decay threshold, so freshness produces a new reproducible manifest rather than mutating an old one
edges.why_related: decay-driven re-pulls keep the map fresh while reproducibility requires pinning a frozen snapshot; freshness and determinism conflict
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the attention web

edges.resolution_rule: keep the head/tail cutoff to stay finite but require COVERAGE_VALIDATION to document the count and aggregate weight of omitted tail places, so finiteness never silently hides material long-tail attention
edges.why_related: the head/tail cutoff trims the long tail to stay finite while completeness validation wants full coverage; per Anderson 2006 the omitted tail can hold material attention
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the attention web

conflict_axes.name: platform_visibility_vs_true_salience
conflict_axes.description: Public signals measure what a platform surfaces; correcting for skew estimates true regional attention but needs an uncertain demographic baseline.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the raw metric auditable; apply correction as a documented adjustment layer

conflict_axes.name: greedy_salience_order_vs_bounded_frontier
conflict_axes.description: Decreasing-salience traversal wants to keep going; the finite frontier bound forces termination and can strand structurally important low-salience bridges.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: raise a documented defeater when a bound would strand a high-betweenness bridge

conflict_axes.name: freshness_vs_reproducibility
conflict_axes.description: Decay-driven re-pulls keep the map current while reproducibility requires a pinned frozen snapshot.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-pull into a new versioned manifest rather than mutating an old snapshot

conflict_axes.name: head_cutoff_vs_long_tail_coverage
conflict_axes.description: A head/tail cutoff keeps the web finite but the omitted long tail can hold attention rivaling the head (Anderson 2006).
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: document omitted-tail count and aggregate weight at validation

conflict_axes.name: per_capita_vs_mass_attention
conflict_axes.description: Per-capita normalization lets small intense places compete but can erase the genuine mass-attention advantage of large hubs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: report both normalized and absolute scores; rank on the goal-aligned one

conflict_axes.name: strict_hierarchy_vs_diaspora_bridges
conflict_axes.description: Single-parent containment keeps the universe finite and acyclic; diaspora bridges capture real cross-border attention but risk re-introducing cycles.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add bridges as non-containment edges only; never re-parent a region

conflict_axes.name: uniform_topk_vs_hub_heterogeneity
conflict_axes.description: A uniform top_k bounds fan-out but ignores that true scale-free hubs legitimately have more salient neighbors than leaves.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow a higher k for nodes whose degree exceeds a hub threshold

conflict_axes.name: central_place_prior_vs_observed_virality
conflict_axes.description: Christaller's hierarchy predicts higher-order places dominate hinterlands, but social-media virality can invert parent-vs-child salience.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the prior as a checkable expectation; flag and keep observed inversions

conflict_axes.name: power_law_fit_vs_lognormal_reality
conflict_axes.description: Fitting Zipf/power-law quantifies concentration but many attention distributions are lognormal, so a forced power-law misstates the tail.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run a goodness-of-fit and report the better-supported model with its interval

edge_cases.description: A diaspora bridge re-parents a region, creating a containment cycle that breaks the finite-hierarchy guarantee.
edge_cases.trigger: a bridge edge is added as a containment edge instead of a non-containment cross-link
edge_cases.mitigation: restrict bridges to non-containment edges; assert single-parent containment after every bridge insertion

edge_cases.description: Greedy decreasing-salience traversal hits the frontier bound and silently strands a high-betweenness bridge, fragmenting the web.
edge_cases.trigger: the node budget is reached before a structurally important low-salience bridge is expanded
edge_cases.mitigation: raise a documented defeater when a bound would strand a bridge above a betweenness threshold

edge_cases.description: A signal source rate-limits or rescales mid-pull, silently truncating coverage for a region level.
edge_cases.trigger: Google Trends caps the query window or a follower API paginates incompletely
edge_cases.mitigation: detect truncation, flag coverage gaps explicitly, and never zero-fill missing signals

edge_cases.description: Platform skew is uncorrected, so an already-visible urban English-language place is inflated over a genuinely salient under-covered region.
edge_cases.trigger: signals aggregated without a per-platform skew correction
edge_cases.mitigation: apply documented per-platform correction factors before aggregation

edge_cases.description: The map is served as current after its validity window has elapsed, presenting decayed salience as live.
edge_cases.trigger: signal age exceeds the half-life-derived decay threshold but no re-pull was triggered
edge_cases.mitigation: gate serving on the validity window; queue aged places for re-pull before serving

edge_cases.description: A power-law is fit to a level whose salience is actually lognormal, overstating concentration and mis-setting the tail cutoff.
edge_cases.trigger: rank-size fit applied without a goodness-of-fit test
edge_cases.mitigation: run a goodness-of-fit; report the better-supported model and a confidence interval on the exponent

edge_cases.description: A uniform top_k truncates a true global hub's legitimate salient neighbors, deleting real structure.
edge_cases.trigger: a fixed k applied to a node whose degree far exceeds the hub threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: allow a higher k for nodes above a degree/hub threshold while keeping a global budget

edge_cases.description: The seed region biases the whole web; a different seed would yield a materially different attention map.
edge_cases.trigger: seed chosen without justification against salience and the analysis goal
edge_cases.mitigation: justify the seed against salience and goal; document seed-sensitivity of the resulting web

edge_cases.description: A diffusion forecast predicts a cascade that fizzles, triggering wasted re-pulls of dormant regions.
edge_cases.trigger: an S-curve overfit to a short window mis-forecasts propagation along a dormant bridge
edge_cases.mitigation: score forecasts against subsequent observed salience and recalibrate; cap forecast-driven re-pulls

edge_cases.description: Per-capita normalization erases a megacity's genuine mass-attention advantage, inverting an expected rank.
edge_cases.trigger: ranking on normalized score alone for a goal that cares about absolute reach
edge_cases.mitigation: report both normalized and absolute scores and rank on the goal-aligned measure

edge_cases.description: The head/tail cutoff drops a place that goes viral days later, and the omission was undocumented.
edge_cases.trigger: an undocumented cutoff threshold excludes a sub-threshold place
edge_cases.mitigation: document the cutoff and omitted-tail weight; monitor near-cutoff places for diffusion-predicted rises

edge_cases.description: A run is irreproducible because a signal snapshot was not pinned and a random tie-break varied.
edge_cases.trigger: live signals and unfixed tie-breaks used instead of a pinned, versioned manifest
edge_cases.mitigation: pin signal snapshots, fix tie-break seeds, version all parameters in a run manifest

workflow.description: Enumerate the finite country>state>city hierarchy with market tiers and assert single-parent containment.
workflow.gate: every place has exactly one parent and the node set is finite

workflow.description: Specify the weighted salience formula over named public signals with documented units and weights.
workflow.gate: salience is computable and reproducible from named public sources

workflow.description: Pull raw public signals with source id, timestamp, and access method for every region at the seed level.
workflow.gate: each datum is provenance-stamped and re-pullable

workflow.description: Attach per-platform skew profiles and correction factors before aggregation; flag coverage gaps.
workflow.gate: each platform signal carries a documented correction factor

workflow.description: Normalize scores across unequal-size regions (per-capita / z-score) so levels are comparable.
workflow.gate: equal per-capita attention yields equal normalized scores

workflow.description: Fit the Zipf rank-size distribution with a goodness-of-fit and report the exponent with an interval.
workflow.gate: the fit reproduces and passes the tail goodness-of-fit threshold

workflow.description: Select and justify the seed region against salience and the analysis goal; confirm signal coverage.
workflow.gate: seed is justified and has full signal coverage at its level

workflow.description: Expand the salience-keyed frontier in strictly non-increasing order with deterministic tie-breaking.
workflow.gate: expansion order is non-increasing and reproducible

workflow.description: Apply frontier cap, per-node top_k, node budget and max depth so traversal terminates finitely.
workflow.gate: traversal terminates within budget; cap breaches raise a defeater

workflow.description: Insert cross-border bridge edges for salient diaspora communities as non-containment links only.
workflow.gate: no bridge re-parents a region; containment stays acyclic

workflow.description: Queue half-life-driven re-pulls for places whose signal age exceeds the decay threshold.
workflow.gate: every over-aged place is queued before the map is served as current

workflow.description: Pin a reproducible manifest and certify finiteness, seed-reachability, salience-order, cutoff documentation, and validity window.
workflow.gate: all completeness, reproducibility, and validity-window checks pass

dominance_rules.rule: REGION_TAXONOMY must define a finite single-parent hierarchy before SALIENCE_METRIC scores any place
dominance_rules.rationale: scoring an unbounded or multi-parent place set makes the web infinite or cyclic
dominance_rules.trigger: salience scoring begins without a closed hierarchy
dominance_rules.action: block scoring until containment and finiteness are asserted

dominance_rules.rule: SAMPLING_BIAS correction must be applied before SALIENCE_NORMALIZATION compares regions
dominance_rules.rationale: normalizing uncorrected platform-skewed signals propagates visibility bias into every rank
dominance_rules.trigger: normalization runs on raw un-corrected signals
dominance_rules.action: require documented per-platform correction factors first

dominance_rules.rule: EXPANSION_FRONTIER must expand in strictly non-increasing salience order with deterministic tie-breaking
dominance_rules.rationale: non-decreasing or non-deterministic order makes the web irreproducible and misorders attention
dominance_rules.trigger: a lower-salience node is expanded before a higher-salience one, or ties break randomly
dominance_rules.action: reject the expansion and restore decreasing-order popping

dominance_rules.rule: DEPTH_BREADTH_BOUNDS caps must be set and active before traversal starts
dominance_rules.rationale: an unbounded frontier lets the long tail explode the node set and traversal may not terminate
dominance_rules.trigger: traversal begins with no node budget, top_k, or max depth
dominance_rules.action: require explicit caps before the first expansion

dominance_rules.rule: DIASPORA_BRIDGES may only add non-containment edges and must never re-parent a region
dominance_rules.rationale: a containment-altering bridge re-introduces cycles and breaks the finite-hierarchy guarantee
dominance_rules.trigger: a bridge edge would change a region's parent
dominance_rules.action: reject the bridge and raise a containment defeater

dominance_rules.rule: STALENESS_REVISIT must queue any place past its decay threshold before the map is served as current
dominance_rules.rationale: serving decayed salience as live presents a confidently wrong stale map
dominance_rules.trigger: the map is served with a place whose age exceeds its validity window
dominance_rules.action: block serving and queue the over-aged place for re-pull

dominance_rules.rule: RANK_SIZE_DISTRIBUTION must pass a goodness-of-fit before its exponent drives LONG_TAIL_CUTOFF
dominance_rules.rationale: a forced power-law on lognormal data mis-sets the head/tail cutoff
dominance_rules.trigger: the cutoff is derived from an unvalidated power-law fit
dominance_rules.action: require a goodness-of-fit test and report the better-supported model

dominance_rules.rule: REPRODUCIBILITY must pin the signal snapshot and parameters before COVERAGE_VALIDATION certifies the web
dominance_rules.rationale: an unpinned run cannot be reproduced or audited, voiding the validation
dominance_rules.trigger: validation requested on a run with live or unversioned inputs
dominance_rules.action: require a pinned versioned manifest before certifying

dominance_rules.rule: COVERAGE_VALIDATION must document omitted-tail count and weight before the web is accepted
dominance_rules.rationale: a silent cutoff can hide long-tail attention that rivals the head
dominance_rules.action: fail acceptance until the omitted tail is documented

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not score salience before the region hierarchy is finite and single-parent; re-scoring after a hierarchy change reworks the whole web
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full re-score after a late hierarchy redefinition

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not normalize or rank on uncorrected platform-skewed signals; un-baking bias from finished ranks requires re-scoring everything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-ranking the entire web after discovering a platform tilt

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not start traversal without active depth/breadth bounds; adding bounds after an unbounded blow-up means discarding the runaway web
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discarding an exploded long-tail traversal and restarting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add diaspora bridges as containment edges; untangling a cycle later requires a graph surgery and re-traversal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-traversing after a containment cycle is found

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not serve a map without its validity window; retrofitting decay tracking after serving stale data means re-pulling and re-scoring
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency re-pull after a stale map is published

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not derive the tail cutoff from an unvalidated power-law fit; a wrong exponent forces refitting and re-cutting the tail
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-cutting the head/tail after a lognormal fit is found better

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run without pinning the signal snapshot and parameters; an irreproducible run must be re-executed from scratch to audit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the full pipeline to reproduce an audited result

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize the seed before its salience and goal-fit are justified; a late seed change re-anchors and re-traverses the whole web
anti_rework_rules.prevents: complete re-traversal after a seed is changed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a containment cycle or multi-parent region is detected after a bridge insertion
iteration_protocol.action: reject the offending edge in DIASPORA_BRIDGES and re-assert single-parent containment in REGION_TAXONOMY

iteration_protocol.trigger: traversal fails to terminate or the long tail explodes the node set
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the caps in DEPTH_BREADTH_BOUNDS and the per-node cutoff in TOPK_FANOUT

iteration_protocol.trigger: a structurally important bridge is stranded below the frontier cutoff
iteration_protocol.action: raise the bound defeater in EXPANSION_FRONTIER and re-check hub identification in SCALE_FREE_LINKAGE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a stale map was served past its validity window
iteration_protocol.action: lower the decay threshold in STALENESS_REVISIT and re-estimate the half-life in ATTENTION_HALF_LIFE

iteration_protocol.trigger: platform-skew bias is found in the final ranks
iteration_protocol.action: recompute correction factors in SAMPLING_BIAS and re-normalize in SALIENCE_NORMALIZATION

iteration_protocol.trigger: a goodness-of-fit rejects the power-law for a level
iteration_protocol.action: refit in RANK_SIZE_DISTRIBUTION and re-derive the cutoff in LONG_TAIL_CUTOFF

iteration_protocol.trigger: a run cannot be reproduced from its manifest
iteration_protocol.action: audit pinned inputs and tie-breaks in REPRODUCIBILITY and re-run COVERAGE_VALIDATION

priority_rationale: REGION_TAXONOMY and SALIENCE_METRIC are foundational; sourcing/bias/normalization make scores trustworthy and comparable; rank-size, scale-free and central-place structure characterize concentration; seed, frontier and bounds drive the finite decreasing-order traversal; half-life, diffusion and re-pull keep it current; reproducibility and coverage validation close the method last.
